scope: Elimination backend used for Lemma 2. Padding with a zero preserves the old factor entries. Materialized tables preserve values, and the deterministic first nonzero pivot scan detects exactly the nonzero rows.
Lemma 2 uses diagonalization to split the two-site tensor. This implementation instead constructs an exact rectangular rank factorization by pivot elimination over a field with exact zero tests.
Eliminating a nonzero pivot strictly reduces the row-space dimension. The number of returned rank-one components equals the input rank, including for singular and zero matrices.

For an r by c dense matrix, pivot scans and the cached residual updates charge at most rc+r²+2r²c field operations and equality tests. This supplies the cubic refactorization cost used in the two-site update.
Lemma 1, Eq. (16). Replacing the addressed site by the one-qubit matrix applied to its physical index implements the gate for arbitrary left and right environments.

Lemma 2, Eq. (22). Contracting the two current sites and then applying the two-qubit gate gives every coefficient of the updated two-site tensor. Intervening bond weights are absorbed into the input sites.

Lemma 2, Eqs. (21)–(27). A pivot-based split reconstructs every gate-transformed coefficient. Its minimal bond is exactly the updated coefficient-matrix rank; in independent outer frames this is the full physical cut rank.
Lemma 2. With all three input bonds at most χ, contraction, gate application and exact pivot refactorization charge at most 24χ³+40χ² scalar operations and exact zero probes.
Eq. (4). An open n-site qubit chain of peak bond χ stores at most 2nχ² scalar tensor entries.
Theorem 1, adjacent-gate execution. Updating any addressed pair and repeating for a finite sequence gives on every bit string exactly the amplitude obtained by dense evolution.
Lemmas 1–2 and Theorem 1. A G-gate adjacent sequence with actual peak virtual bond χ charges at most G(24χ³+40χ²) scalar operations. The physical Schmidt-rank justification is proved separately.
Paragraph preceding Theorem 1. Interleaved physical labels enumerate the bra/ket pairs. Cached matrix products and the one-site transfer implement the dense contraction for each local observable.

Paragraph preceding Theorem 1. Right-to-left contraction of any product of local qubit operators is equal to the full sum over pairs of physical basis strings. At maximum bond χ it uses at most n(20χ³+8χ²) scalar operations including conjugations.
Lemma 2. Full rank gives injectivity of the linear maps from the virtual bond labels into a physical-site unfolding.
Lemma 2, Eq. (22). Every two-site physical slice after the update is the prescribed linear combination of the pre-gate slices.

Lemma 2. The rank-revealing split has full rank on both sides of the updated bond. For an invertible physical gate, the old slices can be recovered, which preserves the other two full-rank conditions. These facts maintain minimal reachable bond spaces under arbitrary gate order.
Eq. (2) and Lemma 2. The full-rank suffix and accumulated prefix frame recover the bond dimension from the physical flattening rank of the state at the current split.

Eq. (2) and Theorem 1. For a nonzero product input, invertible adjacent gates preserve full bond spaces. An intrinsic bound on all contiguous physical flattenings then bounds each computed bond throughout the trajectory.

Theorem 1 for nearest-neighbour circuits. Starting with any product of nonzero local vectors and χ bounding the physical ranks at every dense circuit prefix, the explicit simulator reproduces all amplitudes and charges at most G(24χ³+40χ²) exact scalar operations and zero tests for G gates.

Lemma 2. The dense elimination schedule retains one pivot row and column per completed stage and recycles the residual matrix. Temporary tables for an addressed pair require at most 36χ²+4χ scalar slots.

Theorem 1. The complete adjacent-gate simulation schedule, including the stored chain and temporary update tables, uses at most 2nχ²+36χ²+4χ scalar slots. The unit is a field coefficient; binary precision is outside this arithmetic model.

Paragraph preceding Theorem 1. Transfer contraction on the computed chain equals the product-observable expectation of the original dense circuit. Taking a local projector and identity on all other qubits gives its Born probability on a normalized input.
Theorem 1. Simulation followed by a product-observable measurement costs at most G(24χ³+40χ²)+n(20χ³+8χ²) scalar operations, with G the number of adjacent gates and χ the computed peak width.

Paragraph preceding Theorem 1. The measurement sweep retains at most 7χ² temporary coefficient slots. Including the stored chain, the update temporaries, and the final observable contraction, the peak is at most 2nχ²+36χ²+4χ scalar slots, excluding read-only gate and observable inputs.

Lemma 1 and Theorem 1. A one-qubit register uses its ordinary matrix-vector product with eight scalar operations per gate. In a larger register, each one-site gate embeds exactly on adjacent wires as U⊗I or I⊗U; an inverse of U gives an inverse for the embedding.
